title: 2024/05/28 Opinions on the New Layout (ver.2024.11)
text:
Day One is an app I really like and have been using for over 10 years. It's a very good app and an indispensable part of my life. I've written over 4,000 entries so far. Because I want to keep using it, I'm writing my dissatisfaction with the latest update below.

The new timeline layout is difficult to use and not aesthetically pleasing.

Switching between lists, calendars, media, and maps is easier when the options are at the bottom, as it requires less finger movement, and icons can be understood at a glance.
There are too few parts that use the colors unique to each journal, making it difficult to tell which journal you're looking at, so I'd like you to use these unique colors in more places as before.

It's also not good that the number of entries, streaks, etc., are no longer displayed at the top of the timeline. Having to press the book icon in the upper left corner to check this is inconvenient, and it's harder to stay motivated and feel attached compared to the previous layout where it naturally caught my eye.
Due to these reasons, the user experience and operability have worsened, so I strongly hope that the layout returns to what it was before (or, like last year's layout change, make the old design available as an option).

(Translated from Japanese using ChatGPT)

text:
ver.3アップデート以降、以下の問題が発生しています。
（ほとんど制作元に伝えましたが、動画を送ってくれと返信が来ただけのため、放置しています。）

・入力始めの文字が連続して入力される。
（「あす」と入力すると「あああああす」となる）
・フォントタグが見栄えに反映されなくなった。
（一応PDFにしたら反映はされますが）
・複数の写真を一度に添付すると、間に文字を入力するのにいちいち写真を選択＞「insert text below」をしなければならなくなった。
（以前はカーソルの移動で改行を入れることにより、文字挿入できた）
・リンク名の編集ができなくなった。
（別ジャーナルからのマークダウンのリンクだと日時が入って見栄えが悪いので、以前はリンク名から消していた）
・複数写真を一度に添付した後、中途にある写真のメニューが出しにくい。
・iPadで一覧を出しながら文字入力すると、一覧の写真が点滅する。
・画像を選択して出るメニューが、日本語と英語が混ざっていて格好悪い。
・タグが添付メニューの中に入ってしまったため、添付＞タグと、一手間増えた。
・h3タグまでしかメニューになくなった。
（h5だかh6は水色だったので、目立たせたい時に重宝していた）
・アップデート前に画像添付していた内容の、最後の画像の下の文字が勝手に強調（h1かh2だと思いますが）されてしまう。

それまでは気持ちよく日記が書けていたので、何とか対応を急いでいただきたいものです。

I’m not against companies charging for new features, but taking away or restricting features that were part of the premium experience feels misleading. A little transparency and better communication would have gone a long way.

Day One is still a beautiful journaling app, but this change has made me lose trust in the company. I hope they reconsider how they treat their loyal subscribers.

title: Enjoying the update
text:
I too was originally skeptical of being forced into their sync system.  I read their terms of service and frankly some of the language was frightening, but I had a couple email exchanges with their extremely responsive customer service and I was satisfied they could not use my private entries in the future.  I've been using for two months now and their sync service is fantastic.  I had period issues with iCloud with Day One Classic, but I've never had an issue so far syncing between my iMac, iPhone, and iPad.  

The bottom line is that for YEARS I struggled to consistently journal - since getting Dayone in 2012, and now Dayone 2 - I journal more than I have in my entire life.  It is awesome for capturing moments and recording my life.  I know some day there won't be a price you can put on having these entries.  It's so easy to capture photos in DayOne 2 and being able to have multiple photos in an entry is awesome.  

If your nervous about their sync, just read the news, it's a risk we all take using the cloud, but to me the trade off is that I'm building a lifetime of memories with this app.

Update MANY years later - I wrote the above a long time ago. I’ve been using this app daily and haven’t missed a day since 2015. The new conversation element is amazing to me. It helps me journal throughout the day more instead of trying to remember the whole day. Quite frankly the AI asks some very insightful questions that help me go deeper and have really improved my entries. I’m hoping eventually they will add the ability to use AI to “converse” with your older entires like “hey how did I handle this previously . . . “.

UPDATE 6/11/2026 - after giving original plus members (I’ve been using the journal since 2012) the daily chat for about the last 8 months the tiers changed with no notice or warning.  Went to use it today and see now I’m “silver” and have to upgrade to use it. I get it, apps need to make money but it’s a shame is the same old methods - hook you on the service for some indefinite period of time then take it away.  Not a lot of loyalty for long time subscribers.  I feel like that is disappointing. Even changing the tiers and not keeping it the same. Might be time to look for other options or use apples.

Really a shame they just don’t have as much loyalty toward their subscribers and users that have been here since well Day One.  Pun intended. title: Paid 10 years loyal, day one  left me locked out with no help
text:
I’ve been a Day One user for nearly ten years, and I’m extremely disappointed with what’s happening now.

I’m a paying subscriber, but I suddenly can’t log in at all. My password is correct, yet the app keeps rejecting the login. Even worse: when I try to reset my password, I never receive the reset email—so I’m locked out with no practical recovery path.

I contacted Tech Support, and for days there was no real response. I received an automated message implying they “didn’t receive my email,” even though my email system clearly shows it was delivered. When a human finally replied, the response didn’t address my situation and felt like they hadn’t read my message carefully. After I explained everything again, I got another automated “we didn’t receive your email / do you still need help?” message—basically sending me in circles.

This experience makes the company feel unreliable. And for a journaling app—where users store highly personal, irreplaceable memories—trust is everything. If access can break and support can’t resolve it, that’s a serious risk.

At this point, I’m forced to look for another platform, and I can’t recommend Day One to others unless they dramatically improve account recovery and customer support.

title: Half Liquid Glass, Half iOS 18
text:
December 2025:
I’ve used Day One for ages now (over a decade?) and it’s been a great experience.

However it needs further updated with Liquid Glass and other design elements in iOS 26.

I’m glad the keyboard is there as that’s one of my favorite redesigns, and something about it feels slightly more useful/functional than iOS 18. The new lower bar/selector is there, and the Journals pop-up menu is super nice (though why isn’t the half-sized menu translucent like in Maps), but that bar is about it.

The handy Plus button for creating an entry is just asking for Liquid Glass, instead of that old iOS 18 flat style. Things already updated their Plus button. It’s a very minor detail, yet it’s an object that’s always seen.

And what’s bothering me the most is the headers, inside entries themselves and when scrolling through journal entries. The headers are too “hard” and large and obtuse, a relic of iOS 18. They need to adopt the tinted and blurred headers for iOS 26, or something very similar that honors the journal’s color. Entries will look amazing with that new UI ambiance. For inspiration, simply look at Apple Journal.

The text modifier bar that shows above the keyboard when entering text also could be updated to be more similar to Apple Notes. People whine that no real new features were provided with iOS 26 or that the redesign is useless, but this dynamic bar in Notes has been superbly useful. I use Notes everyday and it’s so much better than in iOS 18, in a way that I didn’t even know I needed. iOS 18 Notes was fine, but iOS 26 Notes is smart. Day One could use a smart text entry bar, instead of hiding all the main text options in the Aa menu.

Also, seeing my old review from years ago, I don’t believe Day One updated the Watch app to be able to view entries. This makes no sense, and in light of now having Apple Notes on my Watch, is perhaps unacceptable.

I ditched Evernote years ago due to the nonsense the new owner pulled, replacing it with Anytype.

I’ve eyed the Apple Journals app a lot… Something about it calls to me. It’s so elegant with its iOS 26 implementation and feels inviting. I’m not sure it’s feasible for me to switch from Day One to Journal (with a couple thousand entries in multiple journals and no import function in Journal), and I’m not sure I even want to do that — but basically I wish I were writing my entries in the Journal interface right now. Because it’s fully up to date in design, and Day One is not. I don’t think you’ve half-assed it, but it does feel half done, half undone.

I also love Journal’s main screen dashboard so much, with the Insights and Places. Day One has its version in the More tab, but I’m sort of wondering why it’s been relegated to third class citizen as the third button. I can envision a nice welcome/dashboard screen in Day One being first, with a plus button to rapidly make an entry, instead of the first view being the scroll of entries. Like, why is the Streaks overview hidden down at the bottom of the third tab?

Speaking of entries, I also love Journal’s way of depicting entries with photos in the scroll view; Journal handles this in a more inviting way by making them large, and the entries are rounded instead of Day One’s arcane hard edges. I feel like Day One could have two view options, the current email-style list and one which is more dynamic with the content inside, when it includes photos or whatever. 

Journal also highlights music for example, and I’m not sure Day One can even present a song as an object insofar as I’ve seen; it’s only possible to add it to the entry metadata, tucked far away in the Entry Info menu… Really? Day One should handle media more dynamically and more elegantly. The current implementation is a very old style of iOS/app design, where apps were just a screen with a simple header and only text as the content. But we’ve come a long way since that.

I don’t need Day One to lose its identity and look just like Journal. But I absolutely want Day One updated to iOS 26 UI/UX standards and sensitivities. There’s a trend of first party apps looking and feeling better, especially with iOS 26’s massive changes in design. And similarly there’s a toxic trend of third party apps resisting new iOS ideas, wherein I develop frustration and impatience when my most used third party apps can’t be bothered to get with the times, times which I quite enjoy and which are here to stay and are going to evolve along this trajectory, no matter who dislikes it. 

I understand Day One may still be working to implement changes in a way that honors its own branding and style, but if a year goes by and iOS 18 elements are still lingering around, well that starts to make an app feel anti-Apple, and I didn’t buy into the Apple ecosystem to utilize apps which exploit my usage and money only to resist the environment they’re benefiting from. And there are a handful od party apps like this, particularly Bearable’s utterly obnoxious proprietary design and behaviors (and lack of basic iOS functions like Search/highlight). If you want to see design done bad on iOS, in a way that pretends to look good until you use it and realize how odd it is (not even mentioning the bugs they always have), just to try Bearable.

For a third party app that does its own design right while honoring iOS sensitivities, look at Things. May all third party apps who don’t want to look like a first party app look to Things for inspiration.

I just don’t want Day One to become a relic. It lived through iOS 7 I believe, and I very much look forward to it not just living through iOS 26, but thriving in design, implantation, and overall UX/ambiance.

Day One is where we spend time with our most personal contemplations. It should be a modern and elegant space. I think if you commit to it, Day One can be way nicer than Journal, not just in having more features, but in elegance and ambiance.

title: Fallen behind other apps with more features
text:
I’ve been using Day One since the beginning. They have fallen behind some other journaling apps with more customizable template options such as formatting tables without using Markdown and show no sign of motivation to add these features. Instead they’re focusing on adding fluff—things that take little development effort, like more journaling prompts. This allows them to show they’re regularly updating the app, though it doesn’t address missing features. Eventually they’ll lose people over those missing features like more customizable formatting. 

Rather than easy formatting of posts, you have to use Markdown. And now, without any apparent notification to their users—users who used Markdown as Day One’s only way to create a table in an entry—they no longer even support printing of tables made with Markdown. 

I’m starting to think that Day One just doesn’t have good enough developers who can make significant improvements to their app. I’m about to not renew my Premium membership, and I’m looking at their competitors who are offering more features, too. 

Day One, get it together and make some significant changes your users want or you’ll lose longtime users (as well as prospective users) to your competitors. You’ve been riding on your early success far too long. Also, the price of Premium for Plus users should not be the same as for those who are just starting with your app. You literally wouldn’t exist if it weren’t for your Plus users who were there when nobody knew who you were.

I have loved using Daylio consistently for years. I love all of their updated and additional customization. I love the layout and I love the concept. I’ve used it to journal my habits and track my inner thoughts…

title: Pls Daylio Read this
text:
I’ve been using Daylio for over 2 years and it contains some of the most important memories of my life. I trusted this app with very personal moments, including audio recordings, photos, and journal entries.

Unfortunately, there are serious issues on iPhone that need improvement. When I receive a phone call while recording an audio entry, the recording gets interrupted or cut off. On top of that, the iCloud backup/sync system does not feel safe or reliable enough.

When my iCloud storage became full, I didn’t lose just 1 or 2 entries — I lost around 200 entries containing audio recordings, pictures, texts, and memories collected over years. After upgrading my iCloud storage and syncing again, most of those older entries disappeared permanently. My text entries partially remained, but many audios and attached memories were gone.

For an app based on preserving personal memories, there should be much stronger protection against data loss, especially with iCloud syncing on iPhone. Users should have:

* safer backup systems,
* recovery options,
* better warnings before syncing overwrites data,
* and protection for audio recordings.

This app means a lot to me, which is why losing years of memories has been heartbreaking. I really hope the developers improve backup security and data recovery for long-term users.

title: It’s fine I guess
text: The app is at face value very good for daily journaling and reminders to do so. However, once you delve further in, you realize the daily challenges are mundane and often outside the realm of accessibility. My most recent before deleting the app was “take a bubble bath,” though I have no bathtub and no way to do so. Along with the challenges seeming useless from a mental health improvement standpoint, there are also a lot of misleading quotes. As someone who prefers their mental health to be guided by enlightened and trained individuals, I would not count Jordan Peterson among those who I am willing to take “positive thinking” advice. There was a shocking amount of negativity inside this app within these quotes. Considering the claim is that this is an AI journal, my hope was that there was a way to train the AI to show me things I like seeing, but instead I just have to suffer through the quotes that pop up on the widget until they go away. Overall the app itself functions fine, no bugs or glitches that I noticed, but I would want to see some improvements before considering using this app again.

title: Subscription Spam Kills UX
text:
As a first-time user who just wanted to learn more about and explore the app, the first five or ten minutes with it was awful and frustrating.

I just wanted to see the interface and determine whether or not I might like it.  

Instead, I got hit with a bunch of popups, subscription paywalls, rating requests, and more *constantly* within the first five minutes — to the point that this “mental health companion” app was actively fighting me while I was trying to figure it out.

I get that subscriptions are important.  I don’t even mind paying for something I like.  But when I’m spammed so much in the first few minutes that I can’t even figure it out, the ask comes across as greedy and unhelpful.

Once I cleared the constant popups, I tried to click around and gain a better understanding of how the app functions.  Nope:  More popups and paywalls.

Based on other reviews, some users are having better luck.  I still don’t know if this app is for me … but after all the paywall spam, I have no interest in continuing.

Devs, please consider implementing a better onboarding flow for users and asking for money *after* someone has a chance to get their bearings.

title: Not super helpful if you are neurodivergent
text: I tried this app to help me regulate and work on developing healthy habits and mindfulness to start and end my day.  I have ADHD and my brain struggles to “boot up” in the morning and “shut down” at night. Asking “what do you plan to do today?” is a great prompt for many, but it is completely unhelpful first thing in the morning when my brain is stuck and unable to start any executive functioning tasks, especially task initiation. Also, the mood thing was tricky for a literal thinker - when I wake up I am not usually sad or mad, I tend to disassociate until my brain fully warms up, so not only can I not pick an accurate mood, I don’t honestly know how I feel about it. I am sure these are great features for people with typically-working brains, but for non-neurotypical brains they were in fact, the opposite. I really do like the concept, it just seems too “one size fits all” for me.

They have you open the app, create your character/critter or whatever, set up your profile, enter your name and information, take a whole quiz and THEN tell you need to pay for a subscription to access the app and its contents. And it looks like they’re pushing a yearly subscription too. Who is actually paying for all this? 🤣

I won’t even be taking my free 7 DAY trial because that’s exactly how they get people. You forget to cancel,  and suddenly you’re being charged for something you didn’t even intend to pay for. So nope! I’ll be deleting the app.

text:
finch is probably one of the worst additions to the adhd “productivity” apps. 

what do you mean, it’s “not overwhelming”?! it’s actually meant to help with adhd?? marketing apps like this leads to excessive burnout and declines in mental health and productivity. finch legit sent me down a spiral i had to work out with my therapist for months. 

i had this app for YEARS and would get overwhelmed and burnt out consistently. it gamifies the whole situation. 

you want more gems to add accessories to your bird, so you make more tasks bc ur tired of waiting every day. this is for adhd. so they should account for that, right? nope! now i have 30 tasks. i don’t do any of them. it’s way too overwhelming to keep up with anything. 

i see the friends feature. i get excited. i add all these friends. all of the friends send me gifts every day! i get overwhelmed. feel guilty about not sending gifts to people i don’t even know. i don’t check it now because it’s too much. 

all the notifications are stacking up. i have to take more and more effort to keep up with this stupid app that’s supposed to make things easier! so i delete the whole thing. finch is probably one of the most overhyped apps to recommend. cmon. do better, please. i trusted you.

title: 利用規約などもちゃんと読めるようにしてほしい
text:
とても良さそうなので使いたいのですが、利用規約やプライバシーポリシーの内容を確認しようとすると、英語のPDFファイルしか開けないので読めません。
せめてテキストデータやWEBページであれば、Google翻訳で読めるのに、残念です。（スクショして翻訳するのはさすがに文量が多すぎて諦めました）

title: 課金の仕組みが分かりづらく、気付けば2万円超え
text:
自動更新の仕組みや料金、解約方法が非常に分かりづらいアプリだと感じました。

私は普段、iPhoneの「設定」にあるサブスクリプション管理から契約状況を確認していますが、このアプリはそこに表示されませんでした。

そのため、サブスクリプション管理に表示されていない以上、継続課金は発生していないものと思い込んでいました。こうした仕組みのアプリは初めてで、課金されていることに気付かないまま約3ヶ月間も支払いを続けてしまいました。

請求額は7月の初回が2,957円、8月・9月・10月はそれぞれ5,916円。気付かないうちに合計20,705円も支払っていました。

実際に利用したのは数回程度です。

解約しようにも手順が非常に分かりづらく、完了するまでに何段階もの操作が必要でした。

事情を説明して返金をお願いしましたが、2度交渉しても返金には応じてもらえませんでした。

自動更新のタイミングや更新料金、契約の管理場所、解約方法、返金条件など、利用者にとって重要な情報は、もっと明確に分かりやすく案内するべきだと思います。

これから利用を検討している方は、登録前に料金体系と自動更新の条件を十分に確認することをおすすめします。

title: 【注意】無料期間後の自動課金に気をつけてください
text:
無料トライアル期間を目的にインストールしましたが、期間が終了すると自動的に有料のサブスクリプション（定期購読）へ移行する仕様になっています。
解約手続き（サブスクリプションのキャンセル）をストアの設定から手動で行わない限り、[週に〇〇円 / 月に〇〇円] の高額な請求が自動で発生し続けるため、お試しで利用される方は十分な注意が必要です。
アプリ内の退会手続きだけでは自動課金が止まらない仕組みになっている（※または：アプリ内に解約ボタンが見当たらない仕様になっている）ため、インストールを検討している方は、事前に解約手順を確認しておくことを強くおすすめします。

text: 精神的に弱っている時期に利用しましたが、契約内容や継続課金について十分に認識できないまま課金が続いてしまいました。90日プランは契約翌日に解約を申し出て解約できたと認識していましたが、その後再び課金されました。さらに別のLivieというサブスクリプションも請求されていました。3か月後に気づいて返金を求めましたが、30日を過ぎているという理由で返金を拒否されました。私にとっては、非常に分かりにくく、不親切な課金システムだと感じました。心が弱っている時に利用するサービスだからこそ、契約・更新・追加サービスについて、もっと明確に説明してほしかったです。Appleアカウントのサブスクリプションには表示されず、直接ページで有効化してApple payで課金され、継続内容の領収書はメールでは送られてきませんので、最初から支払い情報を渡すべきではありませんでした。

title: DECEPTIVE 4-WEEK BILLING TRAP via Apple Pay - Automated Bot Refusals 【注意喚起】海外アプリ「The Liven」
text:
Stay away from The Liven (Chesmint Limited). They operate an aggressive dark pattern designed to trap users into hidden, overpriced recurring subscriptions.

1. Hidden 4-Week Renewal: They obscure the fact that an initial cheap trial auto-renews into an ongoing 4-week billing cycle. Because it is 4 weeks rather than monthly, I was hit with two separate charges of 5,916 JPY within the very same calendar month (August 2 and August 30, totaling 11,832 JPY).
2. Apple Pay on the Web Exploited: They steer payments outside the App Store directly onto their website via Apple Pay, bypassing standard App Store refund protections.
3. Completely Automated Rejection: When disputing these predatory charges, their customer support ("Ava" / "Ellen") simply uses Zendesk automated bot templates to mechanically refuse any refund, citing their rigid "policy."

Do not enter your payment details. If you have been charged, immediately lock your credit card for foreign/online transactions and report them for deceptive practices.

動画視聴などのお試し登録から、気づかないうちに「4週間ごとの自動更新サブスク」に加入させられるダークパターン被害が多発しています。

・1ヶ月ごとではなく「4週間周期」のため、同じ月内に2回（8/2と8/30など）引き落としが発生（各5,916円、計11,832円）。
・App Storeのアプリ内課金ではなく、Webサイト上でApple Payを使わせてカード決済を走らせる手口。
・返金を求めても「Ava」「Ellen」などのAI/定型ボットが規約を盾に一方的に拒絶。

同じ被害に遭われた方は、カード会社で「海外・ネットショッピング利用停止」を設定するか、カードの再発行を強く推奨します。
#Liven #サブスク詐欺 #注意喚起 #悪質定期購入

Update:

After posting this review, I was contacted by other members of Liven’s customer support team, who agreed to reconsider the refunds that had previously been refused multiple times.

They are now working to provide a full refund for both charges, and I sincerely appreciate the constructive efforts of the support staff currently handling my case.

However, for one of the charges, I was told that the refund apparently cannot be returned to the original credit card. Instead, I have been asked to provide my name, address, and bank account details so that the refund can be made by bank transfer. I am currently waiting for an explanation as to why the refund cannot be returned through the original payment method.

Once the refunds have actually been completed, I will update this review again with the final outcome.

title: Not Worth the Subscription — Repetitive Content and Unclear Renewals
text:
Be careful with the subscription.

I subscribed through their website, so it did not appear in my Apple subscription settings. I also did not receive regular billing or renewal emails, and only realized months later that I had been charged 5,916 JPY every 30 days.

I only used the app for the first couple of weeks, and personally, I didn’t find the content useful enough to continue using it.

I contacted support, but they declined any refund.

I wish the subscription and renewal notifications were more transparent. If you try this app, I recommend keeping a close eye on your membership settings.

title: Scam
text:
I was passing through a depressing period when I was carried away by the announcement. I answered the endless questions until I realized that it was never for free. I canceled the subscription in the Apple Store 
And nothing was there accusing a debt or active status. 

But for my surprise it was still active and taking all my money for almost 6 months! 

When I realized, I tried to cancel again but the site kept accusing errors as an excuse and made it very difficult to proceed. Then I sent a dozens of emails until they responded me saying it was not eligible for refund. I NEVER
USED THIS GARBAGE!

It is sad to see that they may use people in this fragile mental condition to take advantage. Take care and be away of this scam!

title: 絶対に使うな
text:
時間の無駄。人間のフリした得体の知れないアプリの言葉遊びに時間を奪われるだけ。
それっぽい言語のような文字を出力しているのが気持ち悪い。無駄な質問ダラダラと投げかけてくるだけで全く噛み合ってないようなものばかり。

情報弱者や困っている人が引っかかりそうなキーワードで広告を打つという戦略です。 ADHD、先延ばし癖、燃え尽き症候群など検索、視聴履歴に基づいて心理的に脆弱な層に絞ったターゲティング広告で、実は汎用的な自己啓発コンテンツを売る典型的なグロースハック型サブスクビジネスです。

もし本気でADHDの先送り癖を改善したいなら、精神科・心療内科での診断とエビデンスのある治療を受けるのが確実です。アプリはあくまで補助ツールとして無料版程度に留めるのが賢明だと思います。

正直このアプリにお金を払うのはもったいないというか何も得るものはない。詐欺師たちが人間の使う言葉になるように文字をならべる、そういう装置アプリシステムを作って、こう言えばこの人間怒るんじゃないか、喜ぶんじゃないかみたいな。そういう人をバカにしたような浅はかなアプリ。こんなクソアプリで情報弱者から金を奪おうと考えるなんて、やはり世界は腐っている。まさに言葉遊びをさせられるだけ。絶対にこのアプリに金を払ってやっただめだ。このアプリを開発した人間たちはほんとにゴミみたいな人間たちだと思う。ウェブの広告を見てみればわかると思う。とにかく困っている人たちが引き寄引き寄せられそうなそういうキーワードをちりばめた詐欺のような広告。そして運営達は思う、バカがまた釣れた、と。そんな広告に騙されないで欲しい。とにかくこのアプリは絶対使っちゃだめです。トライアルの三日間だけって黙れないで。そのトライアルだけのつもりでもお金奪われる可能性があるから。入り口あって出口なしのアプリの可能性があるから気をつけて。あなたが登録したそのタイミングはシステム的に解約できない仕様になってるかもしれないから。気がついたらカードからお金が引かれてる可能性があるよ。気をつけて他の人も口コミに書いてるように。

title: I'm disappointed
text:
最初にアプリを起動すると、テキストブックを追加課金で購入するよう勧められます。
私はトライアルでアプリを体験してからサブスクリプションを契約したかったので、購入したくありませんでした。しかし、”購入しない”選択ボタンがなかったため、一度画面を閉じてから再起動してこのステップをスキップし、先に進めました。“購入しない”選択肢がないのは不親切だと思いますし、もしかしたら後日請求があるのではないかと心配です。
その後も3番目のステップ”幼少期のトラウマ”のビューに異常があります。スマートフォンの画面が左右にスクロール出来ないため、右半分が表示できません。私はこのことが原因で次のステップに進めませんでした。
このアプリは広告で以前から知っており興味がありました。認知行動療法による先延ばしマインドの解決、トラウマを克服するきっかけを得られなかったことは、とても残念です。

title: 日本語訳がわかりづらい
text:
日本語訳がわかりづらいです。
ところどころ英語が入っています。

あなたの今の気分は？ という質問の回答欄に、『NUMB（Googleで翻訳すると『無感覚』）という意味 』があります。

気分感情に、『無感覚や無感情』っていうのが馴染みがないのでわかりづらい。他にも『愛されている』という選択肢があるけど、それって気分なのかな？と悩んでしまう。
テストも、そんな感じで、『私は感情のバランスがとれた人間だ』という質問に『常にある』〜『一度も』の5つの選択肢から選ぶのですが、質問と回答がアンバランスで使いづらいです。

自分の気持ちを理解し癒してもらうアプリだと思うのですが、逆に悩みが増える。やろうとしても、意味不明なことが多くてやる気が失せる。

コンセプト心理分析のテストもあって内容はとても良いと思うけど、日本語訳はもう少し改善が欲しいです。

あとレビューに返信をしてるのはとても素敵だけど、そこも日本語訳に変換してから届けて欲しい。

title: 退会理由
text:
いくつもあります、もし本当に役立つ人の貢献になるなら下記の改善を。
・まずそもそも、日本語訳がおかしいので、何を言っているかわからない
・機械翻訳、自動生成に頼ってレビューしてない結果、同じ文章が2行続けて表記とか頻繁にある、ありえない
・毎日続けさせるなら、UXをもっと洗練させるべき（タスクの登録とか、前の画面への戻り方とか、スマホアプリの基本を学んできて欲しい）
・何でもかんでも過去のトラウマに紐づけようとするアドバイスへの不信感（単に合理的判断で最終的に自分が不利益を被らないために選択している行動もある）
・ホーム画面の実践で、「アドバイス」のやつだけ、いつも実施してもチェックがつかない（こんな初歩的なバグも直さずリリースしている姿勢に不信感）

ありがとうございました。改善される事を祈っています。

title: Beware of Liven’s Separate Subscriptions and Misleading Cancellation Process
text:
I signed up for Liven in October 2025 and canceled my subscription directly through the app in November 2025. I even received an email confirming the cancellation. Despite this, Liven continued charging me for nearly a year without my knowledge.

When I discovered the charges and contacted customer support, I was told that Liven apparently maintains two separate subscriptions: one for the app and another for the website. According to their support team, I had canceled the app subscription but not the website subscription.

Here’s the problem: I’ve never used their website, never logged into it, and don’t even have a website login to my knowledge. I canceled my subscription through the very app I signed up with and received written confirmation. Any reasonable customer would assume that meant their subscription was canceled and the billing would stop.

Instead of acknowledging how misleading and confusing this arrangement is, Liven has refused to refund the charges, insisting that I failed to cancel a separate subscription I didn’t even know existed.

Dealing with their support team has been equally frustrating. I’ve had to repeatedly explain the same basic facts, to the point that I genuinely cannot tell whether I’m communicating with an AI system incapable of understanding the issue or poorly trained representatives who lack the authority to resolve it. I’ve now had to threaten a credit card dispute and a formal consumer protection complaint just to get this taken seriously.

My issue isn’t simply the money. It’s the lack of transparency, the confusing subscription structure, and the refusal to take responsibility when a customer provides proof of cancellation.

If you decide to use Liven, be extremely cautious. Apparently, canceling your subscription in the app and receiving a confirmation email doesn’t necessarily mean they’ll stop charging you. Check every possible subscription and monitor your statements carefully.

Based on my experience, I would strongly recommend avoiding this company.

title: Policies that seem harmful to target audience
text:
I subscribed because this app specifically markets itself toward people struggling with memory, mental health, mood, and parenting, including access to “licensed mental health professionals.” Unfortunately, my experience was extremely disappointing.

I submitted a cancellation notice during my first month, but apparently it was never received or processed. The app continued charging me $94 over three 60-day billing periods without me realizing it. The app itself wasn’t working well for me, and during this period I also experienced a serious stroke-like neurological event that significantly affected my cognitive and mental functioning.

By the time I was well enough to take control of my own finances again, I discovered that the subscription had never actually been cancelled. I contacted the company expecting that the circumstances would at least warrant some consideration, but they refused to refund the charges because of their 30-day refund policy.

I understand that companies have cancellation and refund policies. What concerns me is how this particular policy functions when applied to the exact population the service is designed to attract. If you are marketing a service specifically to people experiencing memory difficulties, mental health struggles, and cognitive challenges, then relying on a cancellation system where a missed or unprocessed cancellation can quietly result in repeated charges feels deeply problematic.

To me, that policy feels predatory toward a particularly vulnerable customer base, regardless of whether that is the company’s intention.

I would strongly encourage anyone considering this service to carefully monitor their billing and independently verify that their cancellation has actually been processed. I wish I had known to do that.

text:
My experience with Liven has been extremely disappointing.
I signed up for the least expensive seven-day introductory plan and, after only three days, decided it was not for me and attempted to cancel. I went through the cancellation process, received an indication that my subscription had been cancelled, and received a cancellation-related email. Despite this, I was subsequently charged $39.99 for a renewal I never intended to purchase.

What I find particularly concerning is that your cancellation process appears to be structured in a way that can leave a customer believing their subscription has been cancelled when, according to Liven, an additional step is still required. I consider this unnecessarily confusing and, frankly, a very poor consumer experience.

I have repeatedly explained these circumstances to your support team, yet the responses have simply pointed back to your cancellation and refund policy rather than addressing the fundamental issue: I actively attempted to cancel, believed I had successfully cancelled, and was then charged $39.99 for a subscription I did not knowingly choose.

A company should not rely on a confusing cancellation process and then use that same process as the justification for refusing a refund.

I am extremely disappointed with how this has been handled and would strongly encourage Liven to reconsider both its cancellation process and its approach to customers who have clearly attempted to cancel before being charged.

title: Please  DO NOT BUY!!!!!!
text:
My experience with Liven has been extremely frustrating and disappointing.

During the purchase process, the website was confusing and misleading. I intended to purchase only the monthly app subscription for $39.99, but I was also charged an additional $49.99 for another service that was not clearly explained during checkout. As a new customer, I genuinely did not understand that this was a separate purchase.

I immediately contacted customer support to explain that I wanted to keep my monthly subscription and continue using the app, but I did not want the additional $49.99 service because I had never intended to purchase it. Instead of helping resolve the issue or working with me to keep me as a satisfied customer, they refused to assist and preferred to cancel my subscription altogether.

It’s disappointing that a company would rather lose a customer who was willing to pay for a monthly subscription than make a reasonable effort to resolve a confusing purchase. Their customer service was unhelpful, inflexible, and showed no interest in finding a solution.

If you’re considering using Liven, pay very close attention during checkout. In my experience, the purchase process was confusing, the charges were not clearly communicated, and customer support was unwilling to work with a new customer who simply wanted to keep the subscription they originally intended to buy.

I cannot recommend this service based on my experience

In June, I emailed saying I needed help canceling my subscription. I received a reply that it was fully cancelled and it wouldn’t be renewed. 

In July, it renews. I reply to the same thread from early June that it renewed even though I had confirmation that it wouldn’t.

Terrible customer service in both interactions. 

1. I reached out in June the first time because I recall “pausing” a subscription felt predatory — it wasn’t clear that I could cancel the subscription. So I emailed. I was seeking help. The reply said I was good and wouldn’t be charged. I thought, “Oh! Ok — seemed more convoluted than that.”

2. Today, even though I’m getting refunded, I get a lecture about somehow misunderstanding or misreading the subscription details. Wrong. I knew this back in June that things felt off, so I reached out. Don’t  blame me for your predatory subscription tactics.

This is a backend issue + bad customer service. Get better, Liven.

title: Mostly good, but not good enough
text: Let me first say, for the most part, Liven is an okay app. The overall options are good, though, some of the topics and videos and articles are a bit contrived and lacking in solid depth. But good enough. What tipped the scale for me from good enough to ridiculous is the fact that I must contact customer service to start a new journey in the app. Even though I  finished the journey, I have no options or further instructions on what to do to start a new one. I finally, after a couple weeks of the last lesson being completed and sitting in my daily to do dashboard, I contacted customer service who told me I need to go to them to change it. They further told me that not only can they not “disclose” the full list of journey options, I have to tell them what I’d like to explore so they can unlock a journey. How in the world would I know what journey I want to take without a list of options. They could even have me fill out a questionnaire to determine the next journey, instead of having to contact a random customer service agent who is very likely not a counselor or trained mental health professional. As such, I am not only getting rid of the app and going elsewhere, I felt it necessary to leave this review.

title: Quiz was correct App was harmful
text:
I was taken in by the marketing which really seemed to have a grasp of my issues. How do you calm down your nervous system when you are sympathetic dominant and in a state of fight or flight nonstop, unable to say “no “ to tasks and set protective boundaries. I am the person who spent 30 years lighting themselves on fire to keep everyone else warm. And the Liven quite correctly diagnosed that. And I was hopeful, because I’m at an age now where the adrenaline is damaging my body.
 
Day 2 on the Liven app was all about the science of procrastination and how I could actually be more effective and get more things done and that I shouldn’t think of myself as lazy just because I feel too overwhelmed to do things. Seriously, what???  Complete 180 from the trip’s correct diagnosis. Insulting even. I have never procrastinated because as a child I had to be proactive about everything or my abuser would rage. The adrenaline hit hard after reading that.
 
Day 3. Same damn thing. How to get past procrastination. It’s like telling a runner with a broken leg how to log more miles. 
 
I went to customer service who originally offered to change my subscription to a shorter one. When I accepted they sent me to “the appropriate group” to do that… and “the appropriate group” bs’d me that they couldn’t due to “technical issues” but they gave me a free month (of more insulting lessons, gee thanks) and a free online workbook of “how to avoid negative thinking” 🤣. Passive aggressive much?
 
I finally went and complained on their subreddit. And of course they blocked it from appearing but chatted with me behind the scenes. Sent my comments to their developers for whatever that’s worth. And then I got an email that my subscription was being cancelled and refunded so they that part was good at least. 
  
But if you are in serious need, keep in mind that when I asked if anyone there had mental health credentials all I got was crickets.

title: very good, pricey with limits
text:
I really like Rosebud and actually think the AI journaling experience is excellent, especially the Dig Deeper feature and the ability to customize what the AI pays attention to. That’s why I upgraded from the free trial, then to Thrive 2x, and ultimately paid $59.99/month for Thrive 5x.

The problem is that I reached my entire weekly AI usage limit after roughly a day or two of use.

I use journaling conversationally and tend to talk through things in detail. I did not realize that longer Dig Deeper conversations consume progressively more of the weekly allowance, or that users are apparently better off ending an entry and starting a new one to conserve usage. That should be explained much more clearly before someone pays for the highest-tier plan.

I really want to keep using Rosebud because the actual product is great, but $59.99/month is difficult to justify if a heavy conversational user can exhaust the highest plan’s weekly AI allowance that quickly.

I’ve contacted support and would really appreciate clarification on how much Dig Deeper usage Thrive 5x is realistically designed to provide.

Great app and concept, but the pricing and AI usage limitations need much better transparency.

title: Paywalls ruin the experience!!!
text:
The Good:
When it works, Rosebud has a lot going for it. The concept of an interactive, AI-driven journal that helps synthesize your raw thoughts into meaningful psychological insights, daily goal trackers, and custom reflection cards (like connecting emotional overwhelm to therapeutic frameworks) is genuinely powerful. For anyone who struggles with staring at a blank page or pulling actionable habits out of a chaotic day, the initial experience feels smooth, supportive, and deeply clarifying.

The Catch / The Bad:
Unfortunately, the user experience falls apart when it comes to subscription transparency and usage limits. After signing up for a paid tier (such as the Bloom plan), users may quickly find themselves hitting aggressive, restrictive background limits that drain their monthly allocation within a couple of weeks—or even after just a single deep conversation. Instead of providing a reliable space to process thoughts, the app frequently hits you with walls demanding further upgrades to higher tiers (like Thrive 2x or 5x) just to keep using the features you are already paying for.

The Verdict:
Rosebud has a brilliant core idea, but the execution of its pricing structure and hidden usage caps makes it feel less like a supportive wellness tool and more like a meter running out. If you don't want to worry about rationing your thoughts or feeling like you’re getting locked out of your own account mid-month, it's hard to justify the cost. Not worth it!

title: Potential to be an incredible tool
text:
This app is absolutely incredible in theory. The first couple weeks I used it I was blown away at how much better than my actual therapist it seemed to be. It not being a real person actually helps in some ways because I’m much less worried about judgement and feel more open. Also the frequency I can journal puts this way ahead of my guy I saw once a week. 

However… there are two issues I have with this app in its current state. One significant issue and one annoyance.

Annoyance: the voice transcription feature is great because it feels much more natural to get thoughts out at the speed of talking. However, the “immersion” is immediately broken when you then have to wait for it to transcribe… then submit it… then wait for the response tokens to come in… then wait for the voice model to start reading it. If there was a way to get it closer to the voice experience one has with something like ChatGPT where it feels more conversational I think that would go a long way. 

Significant Issue: the models that are being used in the background are not smart enough. At times they are great if your topics are straightforward. However if there is even the slightest bit of complexity in a timeline of events you have or you dare talk about two topics in a single entry it will crumble. It has no logic at all and often combines events from different stories like my grandmother used to in the later stages of her dementia. This is within a single entry too… this isn’t when it’s remembering events from past entries. And when you are building an app for something as intimate as Rosebud… as soon as the model doesn’t appear to be listening or comes across like an idiot it completely ruins what should be a healing experience. 

The voice feature would be cool but the latter is the real thing that will prevent me from renewing a subscription. If you could please please please use smarter models this app would actually be life changing.

title: Unreliable Voice-to-Text and Data Loss Concerns
text:
I rely on the voice-to-text feature for journaling because it helps me process more freely and removes the barrier of typing, which can feel exhausting and frustrating. Unfortunately, on multiple occasions, the app has glitched and lost my voice recordings. It gets stuck in the loading stage, and I’m unable to recover what I recorded.
This is especially frustrating when I’ve shared something heavy and vulnerable — it’s not easy to say it once, let alone try again from scratch. A journaling app should make it easier to process, not risk losing what I’ve shared. Please make this feature more reliable — it feels like table stakes for an app like this.
I'm also concerned about the app's priority when processing voice entries. It seems like the app might be prioritizing the AI processing of the voice entry over simply capturing and securing the raw audio recording first. Given that voice-to-text technology has been around for quite some time, I would expect the raw entry to always be available, independent of the status or performance of any third-party models you might be using for AI processing. The core function of a journaling app should be to reliably capture and store our thoughts and feelings, and then run any additional AI analysis as a separate job.
The current unreliability of the voice-to-text feature and the risk of losing valuable entries is making me reconsider my subscription.

Once you get into the app it’s a glorified journaling app that mines your data and gives you AI response. You are better off simply getting a book about correcting attachment styles and paying for therapy. This is an expensive and useless journaling app that using misleading marketing that preys on struggling individuals to mine for data while providing trash AI prompts and responses. Save the money and a headache, go buy a book and a journal for less than the cost of this.

title: Bugs making it unusable
text:
I have reported this issue twice to support and it hasn’t been resolved. I haven’t received any troubleshooting or advice though they have been polite and thanked me for letting them know. My iPad is running on the latest OS and is only a couple years old. 

The app incentivizes you to post an entry each day, and if you don’t you break your streak. It also has challenges you can join which are based on entries. 
The AI component that provides insights is based on number of entries. The calendar that charts your mood each day (so you can look for patterns ) relies on daily usage. 

So it’s very frustrating when the app doesn’t accept entries. I will type a whole thing out and tap and tap that accept button and it doesn’t register it. I am ending up having to copy paste it into my notes to try again later (which is where I was journaling before). I have tried turning the iPad, closing out and re-entering the app, and deleting and pasting it in at different times of day in case it’s a loading issue. 

I am dissatisfied with my subscription now. 

The app has a lot of promise. I like the AI component, though the assessments of each entry could be longer and more in depth, which would be cool to be able to toggle. The insights are pretty good. The moods on the calendar are useful visualizations for me trying to spot seasonal or possible hormonal impacts. If this app could sync with health info it might give even cooler insights. 

I dislike the pressure to journal every day and would like to toggle that off. Id like my entries to count towards the challenges I enroll in, instead of having to journal in multiple places. I’d like my phone and my iPad to be connected to the same journal, it appears to not recognize my login even though I use the same email address, so I am only journaling through iPad. 

Currently the only way I can journal consistently that the app accepts is the voice feature. That’s not convenient for privacy reasons.

While $39.99 sounds manageable, it’s really not if you’re struggling and looking for something to help you figure things out. Charging $3.99 a week is INSANE!! That comes out to $207.48 for 52 weeks!! Why not charge $3.99 a MONTH so you still can charge more than the annual but make it affordable to more people who could use the help. At $3.99 a month you would make $47.88 which will get you an extra $7.89 more than if they pay the annual upfront. I’m really disappointed because I can’t see in real-time how the premium compares. Cool idea but the pricing is ridiculous and I don’t like when people get taken advantage of.
